title: Stonebridge Retail - Renewal & Scale Playbook
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift for Q1, piloting private deployment in EU, timeline for contract extension, and a lightweight benchmark to validate 95th pct latency at target QPS. Customer leaning toward a hybrid (dedicated + private VPC) model; procurement requested a redlined SOW and SOC2 + network diagram. Agreed to run a 2-week performance pilot in January.
next_steps: Aisha to send updated pricing addendum and redline-ready SOW by 2027-12-17
Markus to schedule perf pilot kickoff with Rafael for week of 2028-01-08
Diego to share SOC2 report and network diagram link
Customer to confirm internal approve-by date (target 2028-01-19)
action_items: Aisha Patel: Draft and send pricing addendum + SOW (due 2027-12-17)
Markus Chen: Prep perf benchmark plan + test scripts and kpi targets (due 2028-01-05)
Diego Ramos: Share SOC2, ISO certs, and network diagram (link) (due 2027-12-16)
Rafael Mendes: Provision test VPC and provide access details for pilot (due 2027-12-30)
Nina Park: Start legal/ procurement review and flag any required PO changes (due 2028-01-12)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-12-15 10:30 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Markus Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (CTO), Rafael Mendes (Infra Lead), Nina Park (Procurement)

Summary (auto): renewal check-in; discuss capacity uplift, private VPC pilot in EU, pricing amendment and SOW, SOC2 docs, perf benchmarks and timeline.

00:00:05 Aisha: Good morning everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick check in from our side — happy holl — happy holidays in advance. um, we wanted to walk through the proposed scale playbook and confirm next steps for the renewal and the private pilot.

00:00:33 Lena: Yeah thanks, Aisha. we had a sync internally — high level we're pretty aligned on increasing reserved capacity for Q1. main open points are the EU private deployment path and latency budgets at higher concurrency.

00:00:58 Rafael: hey, just to add — our infra team is worried about a couple of things: network egress costs to the EU region and also the initial terraform work to wire up the VPC endpoints. i can take that on but need clear network diagrams and the access matrix.

00:01:22 Markus: totally. we can provide a network diagram and sample terraform modules; we'll also propose a minimal test harness so you don't have to do the full infra up-front. The pilot would run in your EU tenant with a small dedicated pool and a routing policy back to hosted for overflow.

00:01:47 Nina: from procurement, timeline is bigger for us — we need the SOW and pricing addendum early Jan, but if you can send redlined documents before year-end that's ideal. also SOC2 + encryption details are must-haves.

00:02:12 Aisha: understood. Diego will drop SOC2 and the compliance kit after the call. on the SOW we can send a redline-friendly version by Friday.

00:02:34 Markus: real quick on performance: what are your p50 / p95 targets at the workload level? and what's the typical prompt length and KV cache hit rate? these drive kernel selection and batching.

00:02:51 Lena: for chat storefront flows it's tight — p50 around 80-100ms and p95 under 350ms at 120 QPS for 4 concurrent workers, average context 1.2k tokens. cache hit varies but we've seen about 35% prefix cache on the staging traffic.

00:03:20 Markus: got it, those numbers map to an optimized Llama-like variant with quantization; we can show a recommended config that hits p95 under 300ms with dedicated instances plus prefix K-V cache enabled. the tradeoff will be a small cost uptick vs hosted.

00:03:49 Rafael: can you quantify "small"? our finance team needs rough delta numbers per million tokens so we can budget.

00:04:06 Aisha: yes, we'll include a per-token delta table in the addendum. preliminary estimate is a 12-18% increase for dedicated + private VPC vs pure hosted due to reserved instance economics and egress amortization — but that's before we apply the pilot discounts we discussed.

00:04:29 Nina: and if we go on-prem for EU later, how does that change pricing? is there a license or platform fee?

00:04:44 Markus: private on-prem has a platform fee and a support retainer typically; we can outline options: VPC (customer-managed networking) versus full on-prem containerized deploy. on-prem adds an integration and support uplift of roughly a fixed monthly fee — we'll spell that out.

00:05:06 Lena: ok. our security team flagged KMS/HSM requirement for key custody — we need options for customer-managed keys in the EU.

00:05:20 Diego: Redwood supports KMS integrations, customer-managed KMS is available for dedicated and private deployments; Diego: i'll attach the KMS integration guide to the doc pack.

00:05:39 Rafael: great. for the pilot, assume we want to test at 25% of target QPS (so ~30 QPS) and run synthetic plus a replay of last week's traffic to validate latency and correctness. can you run a warm cache scenario?

00:06:00 Markus: yes, plan is: 2-week pilot, week 1 synthetic ramp and warm cache, week 2 replay of real traffic plus fault injection. we'll set KPIs: p50/p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, and model quality checks against your prompt set.

00:06:24 Aisha: timeline suggestion: pricing + SOW by 12/17, SOC2 + diagrams by 12/16, pilot plan by 01/05, pilot kickoff week of 01/08, internal approve-by 01/19. does that align?

00:06:41 Nina: that would work if legal can start review early Jan. one ask — can you add a clause for data residency and audit logging retention in the SOW?

00:06:55 Aisha: yes, we'll add an appendix for data residency, audit log retention (90/180/365 day options) and a fallback policy — automatic routing to hosted if private capacity is exhausted.

00:07:14 Lena: also want to discuss rollback behavior — if you hit capacity limits, how does Redwood handle graceful degradation? we need clear SLAs.

00:07:27 Markus: Redwood can configure automatic fallback to a smaller model hosted tier or queued requests with estimated wait; we can present the SLA tiers: 99.9 latency SLO for dedicated pools and 99.5 for hybrid with fallback. exact wording goes in the SLA appendix.

00:07:53 Rafael: one nit — in our perf lab we use G4-like hardware for early tests; will your recommended kernels match that or do we need to retune?

00:08:06 Markus: kernels are auto-selected but we'll provide recommended compiler flags and quantization profile for G4-esque hardware. if you send the model artifact (or the HF name) we'll validate kernel mapping before pilot.

00:08:29 Lena: we use an open model family internally, variant name is 'sb-retail-v2' — it has custom system prompts. there may be tokenization differences that affect latency.

00:08:45 Markus: okay, please share a sanitized prompt bundle and we'll run a quick tokenization pass.

00:08:57 Aisha: quick check on procurement: Nina, will a PO or an SOW-first approach work better for you?

00:09:06 Nina: SOW-first then PO after legal signs off. also need vendor risk questionnaire answers — can you populate ours?

00:09:17 Diego: yes, Diego will populate the VRQ and send back by 12/16.

00:09:28 Rafael: security question — do you provide audit logs per user session and can those be forwarded to our SIEM in EU?

00:09:39 Markus: yes, we can stream audit logs to a customer-managed endpoint or S3 in the EU region; retention is configurable and we will include sample CloudFormation/Terraform to wire it.

00:09:58 Lena: perfect. also curious about canary rollouts — we want the ability to test new model versions at 5% traffic before promoting.

00:10:10 Markus: that's supported; our rollout system supports canaries, A/B, and automatic rollback based on quality regressions. we'll include the rollout playbook.

00:10:28 Aisha: let's talk about price sensitivity again — if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, can we bake in volume discounts that scale down token unit price over thresholds?

00:10:40 Nina: yes, we'd like the threshold table.

00:10:45 Aisha: we'll add a tiered volume pricing in the addendum: 0-100M tokens, 100-500M, 500M+. also optional burst credits for seasonal spikes.

00:11:00 Rafael: what about overage handling — spikes happen. do you throttle or bill overage?

00:11:08 Markus: both options: throttle, soft-limits with queued requests, or overage billing. we'll recommend a burst-capacity policy: a small pool of spare capacity for short spikes and automatic billing for sustained overages.

00:11:25 Lena: will the console show token-level cost per route and model?

00:11:31 Diego: yes, the Redwood Console has token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards, and alerts. we can enable role-based access for your finance and infra teams.

00:11:45 Nina: that's important. can we get a demo clip of the console focused on cost analysis?

00:11:52 Diego: sure, i'll include a 5-min walkthrough recording.

00:12:00 Aisha: any blockers from your side for moving forward with the pilot timeline?

00:12:05 Lena: main blockers: internal signoffs and access to sanitized prompt sets. we'll prioritize those.

00:12:15 Rafael: i will need the terraform examples and the intended IAM role names — also a short runbook for failover.

00:12:25 Markus: we'll produce a concise runbook and the terraform snippets.

00:12:34 Nina: from procurement, we'll start with SOW review and vendor questionnaire — once we get the documents by 12/17 we should be able to start internal review 01/02.

00:12:47 Aisha: perfect. Sounds like we have alignment. last quick question: competitors — did you evaluate any other vendors recently?

00:12:56 Lena: we looked at OpenAI for hosted, Anthropic for model quality, and a small infra provider called Nimbus Labs for dedicated cheap capacity. leaning toward Redwood for the control and playbook.

00:13:12 Markus: appreciate that. we'll make sure the pilot addresses the concerns and shows the unit economics for a committed plan.

00:13:22 Rafael: one more technical question — what observability hooks are available for request tracing from our app through to model inference?

00:13:31 Markus: we expose trace ids, per-request token timing, and a sampling of model outputs for quality checks. traces can be forwarded to your tracing backend (Jaeger/Zipkin) or S3.

00:13:45 Lena: good. any customer references for similar retail workloads?

00:13:51 Aisha: yes, we'll share two references that run hybrid (dedicated + private EU pilot) — anonymized contact and short case notes.

00:14:00 Nina: thanks. procurement will also want termination and data deletion clauses spelled out.

00:14:07 Aisha: we'll add those to the contract appendix.

00:14:15 Markus: quick recap of technical deliverables: terraform snippets, runbook, perf scripts, pilot plan — due 01/05. Compliance pack: SOC2, KMS guidance, audit log patterns — due 12/16. Commercial: SOW + pricing addendum — due 12/17.

00:14:36 Diego: action items on our side summarized — i'll follow up with a single doc link and schedule the pilot planning call for Jan.

00:14:47 Lena: thanks everyone, appreciate it. we'll try to get the prompt bundles and tokenization notes by 12/22.

00:14:58 Aisha: great. if nothing else, happy holidays, we'll reconvene after you get internal approvals.

00:15:07 Nina: bye all.

00:15:18 Transcript notes: call ended at 11:16am PST. the above transcription includes some imperfectness in model and product names; follow the attached doc pack for canonical artifacts.

00:15:30 End of transcript.
